{{Quote|What happened to this Boushh? He retired?''"<br />"''Quite suddenly. He tried to rascal Black Sun for more credits on a delivery for which there was an agreed-upon contract. That was&hellip; unwise.|Guri, giving Boushh's outfit to Leia Organa|<ref name="SOTE">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' novel]]</ref>}}
'''Boushh''' was a successful [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Ubese/Legends|Ubese]] [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] active around the time of the formation of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. Known for his melee skills and penchant for [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]], Boushh was considered cool-headed in a profession often filled with trigger-happy [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]], and operated as a freelancer traveling from [[Star system/Legends|system]] to system looking for work. He wore a suit of customized Ubese armor&mdash;layers of brown survival material and an optically enhanced helmet which both provided him with protection and obscured his identity. Although he made sure to never officially join the [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]] but unofficially he still worked for them and also worked with Cradossk, Boushh worked for [[Crimson Nova]], a sect of the Guild dedicated to hunting fugitive [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. During the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], he helped hunt [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Kai Justiss]] alongside bounty hunters [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] and [[Breela]].

After that, Boushh began to work mainly for [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], the largest criminal syndicate in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. In [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], he was sent to hunt down [[Kodo Finn|Kodo]] and [[Aleema Finn]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], but was intercepted by Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Drake Lo'gaan/Legends|Drake Lo'gaan]]. Lo'gaan and Boushh fought, but ultimately allied together when hordes of Imperial [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] raided the building. Lo'gaan escaped and Boushh was apprehended, but he was later released. Many years later, around [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Boushh captured a [[Unidentified Nimbanel|Nimbanel]] for Black Sun, but in doing so spent a considerable amount of [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. He bartered with Xizor for a 50 percent greater payment; this was a mistake, as Xizor, feeling Boushh was becoming a hindrance, had his [[Human replica droid]], [[Guri]], kill the Ubese. Boushh's trademark armor was later used by [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] on missions to infiltrate Coruscant and [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]].

==Biography==
===Boushh the bounty hunter===
[[File:Boushh_SWE.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Boushh masked]]
Boushh was an [[Ubese/Legends|Ubese]] from [[Uba IV/Legends|Uba IV]]<ref name="Star Wars Character Encyclopedia">''[[Star Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> who joined the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunting]] profession early in his life, proving a keen combatant and expert hunter. Although he was slight of build, Boushh wore a suit of "armor," which consisted of layers upon layers of brown survival clothing, and an optically enhanced helmet; this helped mold his reputation as a formidable and dangerous hunter.<ref name="SOTES" /> He acquired a horde of facial scars from his adventures,<ref name="EA:P">''[[Evasive Action: Prey]]''</ref> though because he hardly ever took off his mask in public, few ever saw them.<ref name="SOTES" />

Boushh trusted no one, and often kept tabs on his employers, looking for information he could use against them should they attempt to betray him. He made few alliances during his time as a bounty hunter; he roamed the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], working for various different employers, rarely staying with one for more than a few months. He did, however, work alongside several other hunters on occasion, such as the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiee]] [[Snoova]], and [[Beylyssa]], a [[Human/Legends|Human]] female. Beylyssa and Boushh both shared a love of explosives, but their partnership ended violently&mdash;neither of them was badly injured, though. Rumors abounded that Boushh sent much of his profits on to other struggling Ubese bounty hunters. It was surmised by many of his fellow bounty hunters that he was part of a network of elite Ubese mercenary units. However, these rumors were never proved and their accuracy was doubted by many.<ref name="SOTES" />

Boushh also worked as part of [[Crimson Nova]]&mdash;a subset of [[Bounty Hunters' Guild/Legends|Bounty Hunters' Guild]] dedicated to hunting down [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] survivors of [[Order 66/Legends|Order 66]]&mdash;for a time, and hunted [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Kai Justiss]] on [[Garqi/Legends|Garqi]] alongside fellow hunters [[Zuckuss/Legends|Zuckuss]] and [[Breela]] at some point.<ref name="Underworld" /> Boushh's work with the group was limited, though, and he refused to properly join the Guild.<ref name="SOTES" />

===Working for Xizor===
{{Quote|They belonged to Boushh, an Ubese bounty hunter. Boushh was quite good at the trade. He did a lot of contract work for Black Sun. He&hellip; retired recently.|Guri|<ref name="SOTE" />}}
[[File:DrakeSurrounded.jpg|thumb|right|230px|Boushh and Lo'gaan fight off the stormtroopers]]
Boushh occasionally worked for [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], one of the largest criminal syndicates in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]], though he was not formally tied to the organization. In [[18 BBY/Legends|18 BBY]], he was hired by [[Kreet'ah]], a subordinate of the high-ranking [[Falleen/Legends|Falleen]] known as [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]], to kill two [[Omwati/Legends|Omwati]], [[Kodo Finn|Kodo]] and [[Aleema Finn]] on [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. The two Finns had seemingly defeated a trio of Xizor's agents, and he wished them dealt with quietly and efficiently. Boushh infiltrated the Omwatis' abode, destroying a security guard and using a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]] to blast away the outer wall. He was met by [[Drake Lo'gaan/Legends|Drake Lo'gaan]], a fugitive Jedi [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] and a friend of the Finns. The two faced off for a time while another Jedi, [[Zonder/Legends|Zonder]], fled with Kodo and Aleema Finn. Lo'gaan demanded to know why Black Sun wanted to kill the Finns, though Boushh did not answer him. Eventually, their fight was interrupted&mdash;to the duo's surprise and fear&mdash;by a group of [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]].<ref name="EA:P" />

With a common enemy, Boushh and Lo'gaan began to work together against the stormtroopers, fighting back-to-back. Eventually, however, Boushh's twin [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistols]] were carried through the air by [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] by Imperial [[Inquisitorius/Legends|Inquisitor]] [[Antinnis Tremayne]], who had just arrived. Lo'gaan was able to flee, though Boushh was left defenseless against over a dozen stormtroopers, Tremayne, and his fellow Inquisitor [[Lanu Pasiq]]. Tremayne believed that Boushh was in fact Lo'gaan's associate and fellow Jedi, [[Ekria/Legends|Ekria]], in disguise, though he was disappointed to learn what was truly under the mask. Boushh was allowed to leave, and he returned to inform Xizor personally of his failure to kill the Finns. Some time after Boushh returned to Xizor's headquarters, Lo'gaan, Zonder, Ekria, and the Finns arrived to plead with Xizor for their lives. Xizor agreed, for a price, and the two Omwati were allowed to flee to the Outer Rim.<ref name="EA:P" />

===Other hunts===
{{Quote|In certain operations, I've found it useful to leverage the relatives of the target.|Boushh|<ref name="SWGTCG" />}}
Some time later, Boushh was hired to protect [[Herglic/Legends|Herglic]] [[Gambling/Legends|gambler]] [[Narloch]], who had a hefty bounty on his head for theft and fraud, from a group of bounty hunters. Boushh guarded Narloch while he gambled in a [[Casino/Legends|casino]] on [[The Wheel/Legends|the Wheel]], where they were attacked by the bounty hunters. They fled to [[Dalos IV]], though they were pursued; Boushh enlisted the help of several other [[Mercenary/Legends|mercenaries]] in order to protect Narloch, laying traps and explosives for his enemies. The pursuers managed to make their way to Dalos IV, where Boushh engaged them in a firefight in the hopes of allowing Narloch to escape. Instead, Boushh eventually fled, and Narloch was captured.<ref name="ND">[[No Disintegrations (West End Games)|''No Disintegrations'']]</ref><ref>[[No Disintegrations (West End Games)|''No Disintegrations'']] is a roleplaying game adventure, so the exact nature of the events are vague. Boushh is supposed to be used as an antagonist by gamemasters at various points in the game, though because he needed to survive for the events of the ''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]'', ''No Disintegrations'' states that if he is captured or killed, it is revealed that it is an impostor, and not the real Boushh.</ref>

At some point during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], Boushh was hired by [[Administrator/Legends|Administrator]] [[Lenc]] to capture [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]]-allied arms dealer [[Praaelon Di]], after Di sold arms to both sides of a rebellion on Lenc's mining colony on [[Weldii III]]. Boushh researched Di before making a move, and learned that the gunrunner had a number of [[Assassin droid/Legends|assassin droids]] and [[LM-432 crab droid/Legends|LM-432 crab droids]] at his disposal; thus, Boushh hired a number of other bounty hunters to assist him in the hunt. Boushh assembled the team with their abilities in mind, and the end result was that he had a group capable of countering Di's powerful droids. The bounty hunters clashed with Di aboard his ship, the ''[[Tri-Sun]]'', with Di coming out on top.<ref name="unfinished2">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/unfinished2|text=Unfinished Business, Part 2: Well-Armed and Dangerous|int=Unfinished Business (scenario)}}</ref> Boushh then traveled to [[Mine Shaft 342]], Weldii III, where Lenc was overseeing repairs to his mine. Di, with more forces, including Rebel allies, arrived to kill Lenc; Boushh hoped to execute part of the bounty on the arms dealer. However, Praaelon Di was ultimately successful in his efforts, and Boushh did not capture him.<ref name="unfinished3">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/unfinished3|text=Unfinished Business, Part 3: Shafted!|int=Unfinished Business (scenario)}}</ref>

[[File:Boushh-BetweenTheShadows.png|thumb|left|200px|Boushh wielding a force pike]]
Sometime after the [[battle of Talus]] Boushh was tracking [[Corellian Security Force]] operative [[Corran Horn/Legends|Corran Horn]] from the [[Emperor's Most Wanted]], a list of high-paid bounties on important Alliance leaders. He was assisted by another bounty hunter, both agreed that using a direct approach in apprehending Horn would be difficult, Horn was difficult to ambush and even more difficult to deceive. Once the two agreed that Boushh would collect the bounty, he offered to capture Corran's father, [[Hal Horn]], and lure Horn into a trap. The bounty hunters captured the elder Horn and moved him to a secure location, which was soon ambushed by Corran and several other CorSec operatives. However, Boushh's perimeter security alarm gave the bounty hunters the critical seconds necessary to withstand the initial assault, and the battle soon turned into a standoff. The bounty hunters offered to let the elder Horn go if Corran would turn himself over to them. Refusing to allow harm to come to his father, Corran agreed to the ultimatum, allowing Boushh to cuff and capture himself.<ref name="DS">{{SWGTCG|set=Galactic Hunters|scenario=Dark Side scenario campaign}}</ref>

===Demise===
{{Quote|This bounty hunter is my kind of scum&hellip; fearless and inventive.|translated=1|Jabba the Hutt, to Organa, in Boushh's armor|<ref name="Episode 6">{{Film|VI}}</ref>}}
[[File:Boushh-The_Dark_Times.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Boushh in the time of the Empire]]
Boushh continued to work as a freelancer for several years, though by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], he frequently worked for Black Sun, contacted by agents such as [[Chorh-dha]], [[Vimriss]] and other underlings of the [[Vigo/Legends|vigo]] [[Green]], who had criminal interests in that region of space. Per his usual practice, Boushh tried to spy on those agents and probe on their contacts, superiors, and the wider context of their interests, something that was undesireable for the secretive organization.<ref name="bounty">{{WEGCite|story=Bounty's Due|book=Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook}}</ref> He blackmailed a vigo during this time, which earned him Xizor's ire.<ref name="SaV">[[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']]</ref> 

In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], Chorh-dha hired him to capture a [[Unidentified Nimbanel|Nimbanel]] enemy of Black Sun; he succeeded, but to his usual practice, Boushh contacted Black Sun claiming that the hunt ultimately cost him greatly, for he had to use much equipment and technology to capture his quarry; he requested that he be paid 50 percent extra, to which Xizor agreed.<ref name="bounty" /> 

Boushh was staying with the Nimbanel in an old [[Cargo container/Legends|cargo container]] serving as a hovel in the muddy streets of [[Gelgelar/Legends|Gelgelar]] waiting for Chorh-dha. Xizor's [[Human replica droid]], [[Guri]], showed up in the [[Rodian/Legends|Rodian]]'s place and presented him with a metal case supposedly filled with [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]]. Ever paranoid, Boushh frisked Guri, finding no weapons, though he refused to open the case; he wanted her to open it, so that he could keep his blaster trained on her permanently. Guri obliged, and Boushh began to search through the credit chips, but he was momentarily incapacitated when a hidden [[Dinko (creature)|dinko]] bit him. Guri took this opportunity to kick Boushh in the face, snapping his neck. Boushh had crossed the line with Black Sun, with both his demands for extra payment and his blackmailing of a vigo.<ref name="SaV" /> Guri picked up Boushh's body, and the Nimbanel captive, back to Xizor.<ref name="bounty" /> Few knew of his death, though, which would later be used to others' advantage.<ref name="SOTES" />

[[File:Leia_boush2.jpg|thumb|left|200px| Leia Organa disguised as the bounty hunter Boushh.]]
Some time later, Guri gave [[Boushh's armor]] to a leading member of the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]], [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], on [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]], so that she could infiltrate Coruscant to meet with [[Xizor/Legends|Xizor]]. The suit fit Organa perfectly, and she and her friend [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]]&mdash;disguised as Snoova, Boushh's old partner&mdash;used it to get onto Coruscant without arousing suspicion.<ref name="SOTE" /> Organa kept the armor for use on later missions; in [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]], she once again disguised herself as Boushh and brought Chewbacca to [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure's]] [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|palace]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].<ref name="RotJn">[[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode VI: Return of the Jedi'']]</ref> During her time disguised as Boushh, she also participated in [[Jabba's demolition games]], riding a [[Speeder bike/Legends|speeder bike]].<ref name="SWD">''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]''</ref> Organa could speak [[Ubese (language)/Legends|Ubese]], and because the mask concealed her true appearance, none suspected her deception. After she was captured, however, the armor was discarded by Jabba's minions.<ref name="RotJn" /> Despite this, few knew of Organa's ruse, and many suspected that Boushh was not dead, but merely retired.<ref name="SaV" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Chorh-dha thought it would be better to send me. Someone you might trust more.''"<br />[Laughs] "''Yo czhal.|Guri and Boushh|<ref name="SOTES" />}}
[[File:Boushh.png|thumb|right|200px|Boushh in his signature outfit, without helmet]]
Boushh was paranoid and cautious to a fault, and always planned for and expected the worst. He trusted no one, expecting to be backstabbed, cheated, taken advantage of, and lied to at every turn. Boushh allied with no organization, moved on to a new employer every few months; he spent great deals of time searching for information both on his prey as well as his employers, anticipating counter-moves. As for his employers, he hoped to find incriminating items; should someone attempt to deny him his due payment, he would blackmail and threaten them until they paid up.<ref name="SOTES" /> This led partially to his downfall; one of the reasons Xizor had him killed was that the Ubese hunter was blackmailing a Black Sun vigo.<ref name="SaV" />

Boushh cared more about his own life than money, and he had no qualms about turning down a bounty offer which would put him in any considerable danger, even for immense sums of money.<ref name="RES">''[[Rebellion Era Sourcebook]]''</ref> When hired by Narloch, Boushh left the Herglic gambler for dead when he fled Dalos IV, demonstrating that he cared more for his own skin than fulfilling his mission.<ref name="ND" /> Boushh was also notorious for often demanding extra credits after successfully capturing a bounty; he claimed that this was because he had used resources, such as high quality equipment, in tracking them down, though this was often exaggerated.<ref name="SOTES" />

Like most members of his [[Species/Legends|species]], Boushh had a fascination with technology of all sorts. He was known to use a wide array of small, easily concealable gadgets while pursuing quarry, and had a love of all things explosive.<ref name="SOTES" /> He used explosives to make an impression, and played to his reputation for appearing somewhat suicidal, hoping that his targets would give themselves up in the erroneous knowledge that Boushh would blow himself up in order to take others down with him.<ref name="SaV" /> However, he was also talented at close-quarters combat, and often used small blades during his work.<ref name="EA:P" /> Boushh was known to be a fearless and inventive bounty hunter,<ref name="CCG">{{CCG|set=Enhanced Jabba's Palace|cardname=Boushh}}</ref> cool and calculating in a profession of trigger-happy freelancers.<ref name="SWGTCG" />

==Equipment==
[[File:Boushh_BotF_by_Bradbury.png|thumb|left|210px|Boushh with a blaster rifle]]
Boushh wore a suit of customized "[[Ubese raider armor|armor]]," incorporating the traditional Ubese [[Ogygian cloak/Legends|Ogygian cloak]]. He wore many layers of rough survival clothing, light brown in color, with spiked, metal armor on his shoulders, neck, and wrists. [[Shata leather pants/Legends|Shata leather pants]] covered his legs, with traditional cream-colored Ubese boots. Boushh wore several bandoleers, packed tight with small [[ammo pouch]]es that hold explosives&mdash;projectile detonators, [[Flash grenade/Legends|flash]] and [[Stun grenade/Legends|stun grenades]], [[Computer surge exploder plug]]s, intricate [[Timer bomb|detonation timers]] and [[Plasma-burn tape]]s, and [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonators]]&mdash;around his chest, and an [[Ubese clan belt-clasp/Legends|Ubese clan belt-clasp]] around his waist.<ref name="VD">''[[Star Wars: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref><ref name="SOTES" />

Boushh's helmet allowed him to breathe [[Atmosphere/Legends|Type I atmospheres]];<ref name="SOTES" /> without it, such atmospheres would damage his lungs.<ref name="SOTE" /> The helmet also contained an [[Audio sensor/Legends|audio pickup]] and [[Broadband antenna/Legends|broadband antenna]],<ref name="SWCVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> a speech scrambler,<ref name="SWCVD" /> an optically enhanced vision scanner,<ref name="VD" /> and a flash guard visor, which nullified the effect of any [[Stun grenade/Legends|stun grenades]].<ref name="SOTES" /> Boushh always carried numerous weapons with him: a [[Force pike/Legends|force pike]],<ref name="RES" /> a [[Lance/Legends|lance-blade]],<ref name="VD" /> a [[Heavy blaster pistol/Legends|heavy blaster pistol]],<ref name="RES" /> and a pair of melee swords.<ref name="EA:P" /> He was also known to utilize an [[Electrostaff/Legends|electrostaff]].<ref name="Hasbro">{{HasbroCite|set=Saga Legends|pack=Princess Leia (Boushh Disguise)|altlink=https://www.rebelscum.com/TACSLleiaboushh.asp}}</ref><ref name="ESWCaSDC-C">{{SW|url=news/exclusive-star-wars-collectibles-at-san-diego-comic-con|text=Exclusive ''Star Wars'' Collectibles at San Diego Comic-Con}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
Boushh was created for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] in [[1983]]. He first "appeared" in [[James Kahn]]'s [[Star Wars: Return of the Jedi (novelization)|novel adaptation]] of the film; it is not revealed until after Boushh's first scene in ''Return of the Jedi'' that he is in fact Leia Organa in disguise. Boushh's costume appeared again in the ''Return of the Jedi'' film, though, unlike in the novel, his name was never given. He was voiced by [[Pat Welsh]] in ''Return of the Jedi''.

Boushh has been used infrequently for a movie character, only making a handful of other appearances. Boushh was not referenced again until [[1996]], when [[Steve Perry]] used the character for his novel ''[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]'' to explain how Leia got his armor. The ''[[Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook]]'' expanded his backstory.

Several reasons are given for Boushh's death; ''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]'' simply says that he "made the mistake of withholding credits on a job for the syndicate".<ref name="The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire">''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]''</ref> The concurrent ''Sourcebook'' (1996) says that he demanded a higher payment,<ref name="SOTES" /> while the much later [[Scum and Villainy (sourcebook)|''Scum and Villainy'']] ([[2008]]) says that he blackmailed a vigo.<ref name="SaV" />

Leia Organa, wearing Boushh's armor, is one of the playable characters in the [[2000]] video game ''[[Star Wars: Demolition]]''. However, unlike the majority of the characters developed for the game, a winning and losing cutscene for Leia were not added for the character.

[[Paul Ens]]'s ''[[Evasive Action: Prey]]''&mdash;which contains the first image of an unmasked Boushh&mdash;is the only narrative [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] source the character has appeared in alive.
